title: RDW-by-MCV scaling shows no clear incremental walking-difficulty discrimination in two NHANES cohorts
abstract: RDW associations with physical function do not establish incremental prediction. We tested RDW times mean corpuscular volume divided by100 as a dispersion-scaled interaction beyond demographics, BMI, hemoglobin, RDW, MCV and quadratic red-cell terms. Source-only models used 1920 NHANES2007–08 adults aged60+ (346 cases); independent2009–10 confirmation used 1904 adults (354 cases). Source fivefold out-of-fold deltaAUC was-0.000040. Target AUC changed from0.734430 to0.734296, delta-0.000135 (paired bootstrap95%CI -0.000737 to0.000517); Brier loss worsened by0.000023. Joint refitting and a flexible additive spline challenge did not support incremental benefit. This bounded negative result concerns one deterministic representation and fixed model, not all physiological information in red-cell distributions.
